name: PrivescCheck - PowerShell Windows Privilege Escalation Auditor
description: PrivescCheck is a comprehensive PowerShell script that checks for all common Windows privilege escalation vectors: service misconfigurations, unquoted paths, DLL hijacking, scheduled tasks, registry autoruns, credential files, and more. Modern replacement for PowerUp with better detection coverage.
notes:
=== BASIC USAGE ===
  powershell -ep bypass
  . .\PrivescCheck.ps1
  Invoke-PrivescCheck

=== EXTENDED CHECK + REPORT ===
  Invoke-PrivescCheck -Extended -Report PrivescCheck_RESULTS -Format TXT,HTML

=== WHAT IT CHECKS ===
  # Services:
  - Unquoted service paths
  - Modifiable service binaries
  - Modifiable service parameters
  - World-writable service directories
  # Registry:
  - AlwaysInstallElevated
  - AutoLogon credentials
  - Autoruns with weak permissions
  # Filesystem:
  - DLL hijacking opportunities
  - Writable PATH directories
  - Writable program directories
  # Scheduled Tasks:
  - Modifiable task binaries
  - Modifiable task directories
  # Credentials:
  - Cached credentials
  - SAM backup files
  - Unattend.xml files
  - Web.config files
  # Network:
  - Open ports and services
  - WiFi passwords

=== COMPARISON ===
  PrivescCheck:  Most comprehensive, actively maintained
  PowerUp:       Classic but less maintained
  WinPEAS:       C# binary, very thorough, noisier
  Seatbelt:      GhostPack, more post-exploitation focused
  SharpUp:       C# port of PowerUp

recommended.note: WinPEAS for C# binary alternative with similar coverage.
LinPEAS for Linux privilege escalation enumeration.

defense.why_it_works: PrivescCheck systematically audits Windows configuration for privilege escalation vectors by checking file permissions, registry keys, service configurations, and credential storage.
defense.prerequisites: PowerShell execution on target; script uploaded or loaded in memory.
defense.impact: Identifies all local privilege escalation paths; guides attacker to SYSTEM.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1082] PowerShell script execution with enumeration patterns; accessing sensitive registry keys and service configurations.
defense.artifacts: PowerShell script block logging; access to service registry keys; WMI queries for services.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows sourcetype=WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational EventCode=4104 ScriptBlockText="*PrivescCheck*"
| table _time, ComputerName, ScriptBlockText
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceEvents
| where ActionType == "PowerShellCommand"
| where AdditionalFields has "PrivescCheck"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AdditionalFields
defense.prevention: Enable PowerShell Constrained Language Mode; script block logging; AMSI; restrict PowerShell execution policy.

detections.name: PrivescCheck or privilege escalation enumeration script
detections.logic:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName == "powershell.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("PrivescCheck", "Invoke-PrivescCheck", "PowerUp", "Invoke-AllChecks")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
detections.false_positives: Security audit teams running authorized assessments
detections.tuning: Also detect by behavior: rapid enumeration of services, registry keys, and scheduled tasks
